subject: Beginner question on import of data

messages.author: a8b003d0e7a206b0
messages.subject: Beginner question on import of data
parts:
Hello everyone, I'm a CAD/GIS specialist and I'm beginning to use the Distance software for the needs of sea birds survey analysis (which I've never done before), I've run some of the example projects and simulations with R, I'm reading the instruction manual.

I was able to import some of the spatial data (the area of survey, the transects and transect-section midpoints). I have a database from the inventory with the species and the count of the birds, but I cant join them in Distance spatially. Can anyone help me?
BR, Piotr

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Beginner question on import of data
parts:
Piotr

If you are producing estimates of density/abundance for your seabirds using design-based inference, you need not provide geo-referenced data in your Distance project.

If you are performing model-based inference (which I suspect, given you have provided "transect-section midpoints"), there is still no need to provide spatial locations of the individual detections.  I suggest you investigate the structure of the sample project named "Dolphins.dst" to note how those data are organised.

In addition, if you are conducting model-based inference, you will also need to create a prediction grid layer in your project.

I need this data for further processing, in order to see how many birds might have been missed and to calculate the density surface (kriging with spherical semivariogram, which I make in SAGA GIS)
I will be on the seminar in St Andrews at the end of the month , so I can show you how the survey is designed.

Piotr
